sentence: This project studies genes and molecular pathways linked to congenital heart disease using computational genomics, stem cell derived heart cells, and knockout mouse models.
This project builds the ability of a laboratory to test food with microbiological, radiochemistry and chemistry methods.
This project tries to find out how a pathway that tissues use to respond to hypoxia fights damage from hypoxia.
This project studies the molecular causes of hepatocellular carcinoma arising from obesity-induced steatohepatitis in mice and tests combinations of treatments.
This project provides a slide scanner with an automatic loader to give detailed imaging support to users of a core facility.
This project studies how genetic and epigenetic mechanisms decide what specific cell types basal cells in mouse airways turn into.
This project studies how the genome is set up to support normal blood system development and what happens when a controlling protein is lost.
This project offers support with statistics and research design to cancer researchers, from planning a study to analysis.
This project tries to find out how nociceptin opioids released by the central amygdala affect reward processing.
This project studies somatic mutations across human tissues and builds a catalog of them.
This project maintains and develops the frog Xenopus laevis as a research resource, with inbred and transgenic animals, for studying immunology.
This project tries to find genetic links to sleep apnea and insomnia and to sort out subtypes that raise the risk of other diseases.
This project builds a genetic platform to find out how treatment that modulates g-secretase can be separated from its toxic inhibition in Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds a gene therapy that uses gold nanoparticles to insert protective antibody genes into immune cells against viral respiratory infections.
This project builds microscopy tools that watch brain cancer cells and blood vessel remodeling in vivo.
This project holds a workshop to share ideas, tools and digital resources for postmortem research on Alzheimer's disease and related dementias.
This project studies how a protein that modifies mRNA affects the development of acute myeloid leukemia and self-renewal of leukemia stem cells.
This project introduces research in environmental health, including toxicology, exposure science, environmental monitoring and green chemistry.
This project builds a dye-containing contrast agent for photoacoustic imaging to plan and monitor antibody-drug conjugate treatment of triple-negative breast cancer.
This project studies how HIV uses ribosomal frameshifting to make viral enzymes and how this affects its replication and disease.
